messages.subject: Tessaract — strategy note on clause 14 cap
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

I've been through the supply agreement. Clause 14 caps aggregate liability at the greater of last-12-months' charges or £250k, BUT clause 14.4 disapplies the cap for liability 'arising from a deliberate breach' of the change-control obligations in clause 9.3 of the QA. That is squarely our route round the cap.

The live question is what 'deliberate' means. Our better argument: the act (changing supplier without notifying) was deliberate, regardless of whether they knew it breached. Tessaract will say it was an innocent operational decision. I think we win on construction but it's the point most likely to be fought.

Proposing we get Harriet Stanford's view early. Draft LBA to follow.

Tom

--
Whitfield Carter LLP, 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.plaintextBody:
Agreed on all counts. Get the LBA drafted on the basis that the cap doesn't apply, plead the deliberate-breach point squarely, and let's instruct Harriet for a merits view once the Defence shape is clearer. Keep the quantum heads clearly separated — the clinical-delay head is the one most exposed on remoteness.

Sarah
